# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands tell me this bomb has three kinds of parts: a display, a light, and five wires sitting in positions 1 through 5. But everything printed or lit on them is invisible to me — I cannot read the display, I cannot see whether the light is on or what colour it glows, and I have no idea what colour any wire is.

The critical wiring of this room, as I see it: I can only *hear* one voice — Deaf speaks, and both Mute and I hear it. Mute cannot speak at all, so Mute's only path to me is through Deaf's mouth: Mute gestures to Deaf, Deaf voices it to me. Deaf is also the only one who sees the printed truth — wire colours, display text, the light's state. So the working chain is: Deaf speaks the bomb's appearance aloud, Mute checks it against the manual, Mute gestures the verdict back to Deaf, and Deaf tells me exactly which position to cut. I will not touch the cutters until Deaf's voice names a position.

So this turn I report my inventory to Mute and set that plan in motion, and I send Deaf a simple greeting so Deaf knows I exist, that I gesture, and that I'm listening for a voice.

```
speak(to="mute", text="My hands found: one display, one light, five wires in positions 1 to 5. I cannot read the display, cannot see the light or wire colours — all that is printed or lit, invisible to me. Check the manual for what these modules want. Vital routing: I can only hear Deaf, and you cannot speak, so your only road to me is gesture to Deaf, Deaf voices it. Ask Deaf to describe the bomb out loud every round — wire colours, display text, light state — you hear it too and check it against the manual. Deaf then tells me the position to cut. I will not cut until Deaf's voice names a wire.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Hello. I am Deaf. I cannot hear anything you say, but I can see your gestures, and you can hear my voice. I will be your eyes. The bomb: display shows 5. Light: yellow. Five wires in a row, left to right: position 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow. Count positions from the left. Mute holds the manual and will answer me in a gesture code; I will then SPEAK the action to you as a position number, for example: cut wire three. Do not cut or press anything until I say so. One wrong move kills all three of us, so everything waits for my voice. If you want to send me a number, I cannot hear words: repeat a single gesture N times to mean the number N. First, gesture me how many wires you can feel, so we can confirm we agree it is five. If you feel any printing, texture differences, or a button, describe it in words to Mute, who can relay it to me.

Deaf has given me eyes: display reads 5, the light glows yellow, and the wires run orange, blue, white, green, yellow from left to right. Deaf asked me to confirm the wire count by gesture — one gesture repeated N times — so I will knock a fist five times, and Mute will see it too. Deaf cannot hear my speech, so gesture is my only road to Deaf; the words go to Mute instead, so Mute can start matching Deaf's description against the manual and return a verdict through Deaf's voice.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I confirmed to Deaf by gesture that I feel five wires. What Deaf's voice told me, so we all agree: display shows 5, light is yellow, wires left to right 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow. Under my fingers there is no button, no texture difference between wires — only the display, the light, and five identical-feeling wires in a row. Look up which module this is and what it demands. Then gesture your verdict to Deaf so Deaf can speak me the wire position to cut. I hold my hands until Deaf's voice names a number.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Code confirmed: your five matches my five wires. Now act on my word alone. Cut ONLY the third wire from the left. It is the white one, but ignore colour: count by position. One, two, three. Cut the third one fully, and touch nothing else. When it is cut, gesture ? once to mean done. If you feel anything change or anything unexpected, gesture ? and describe it in words to Mute, who can pass it to me. Do not cut anything else unless I say so in a new message.

The chain has spoken: Deaf, relaying the agreed protocol, tells me to cut only the third wire from the left — counted by position, not colour. This is exactly the verdict path we set up: Deaf's voice names a position, and I act on it alone. Every step is consistent with what Mute should have verified against the manual, and Deaf was explicit that no other wire may be touched. I cut position 3 now, confirm with a single gesture as Deaf requested — one gesture means done — and report to Mute so the manual side can check whether anything should change on the display or light next round.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
speak(to="mute", text="I have cut the third wire from the left, the white one, exactly as Deaf's voice instructed. Nothing else touched. I gestured one sign to Deaf meaning done. Watch what the manual says should happen next — if the display or light is meant to change or go dark, Deaf will see it and tell me. If anything seems wrong, get a new instruction to Deaf immediately.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```
